title: The Fastest Thing In Your Body
sources: Nerve signals: the fastest myelinated nerve fibres conduct at up to about 120 m/s, roughly 268 mph (Purves et al., Neuroscience; Kandel, Principles of Neural Science)
Blood: peak velocity of blood leaving the heart through the aorta is about 1.0-1.7 m/s in healthy adults, roughly 2-4 mph (echocardiography reference ranges)
Sneeze: measured maximum sneeze airflow about 4.5 m/s, roughly 10 mph, far below the often quoted 100 mph (Tang et al. 2013, PLoS ONE)
Cough: air can leave the lungs at up to about 50 mph (American Lung Association; cough flow studies report peak velocities of 10-22 m/s)
Pain: slow, aching 'second pain' travels on unmyelinated C fibres at about 0.5-2 m/s, roughly 1-4 mph, so it arrives about a second after the sharp first pain (Purves et al., Neuroscience)
